author: Glenn Kinley
title: Illini hold off Northwestern for sixth-straight win - NewsBreak
text:
By Glenn Kinley ,
11 hours ago
EVANSTON, Ill. (WCIA) – Illinois men’s basketball is still yet to lose in the year 2026.
The Illini beat Northwestern 79-68 on Wednesday, extending their winning streak to six. It marks the first win in Evanston for the Illini since 2022, snapping a three game losing streak in Welsh-Ryan Arena.
Illinois started the game with a 6-0 run, but couldn’t hold it early as Northwestern came back to take the lead early in the first half. However, Illinois rallied to find itself ahead by five, 38-33, after 20 minutes.
In the second half, Illinois would open up its largest lead of the day, 15 points, with 9:43 to play. However, it was anything but simple from there. Illini freshman Keaton Wagler was called for a flagrant foul, then a technical foul was called on the Illinois bench.
Northwestern used the momentum which came with those calls to crawl back within four, trailing 67-63 with 4:57 left in the game.
Tomislav Ivisic was instrumental in holding off the late push from the Wildcats. He hit two three-pointers in the final three minutes, finishing with 21 points. It marks T. Ivisic’s highest scoring output since the first game of the season, when he also scored 21, against Jackson State.
Wagler scored just two points in the first half, but woke up in a big way down the stretch – finishing with a team-high 22 points. Kylan Boswell finished with 13.
Northwestern senior Nick Martinelli, who entered Wednesday’s contest as the Big Ten’s leading scorer, posted 20 points.
Illinois hasn’t lost since Dec. 13, when Nebraska won on a last-second shot in Champaign. Illinois improves to 14-3 overall and 5-1 in Big Ten play with the win. The victory also improves Underwood’s team to 4-0 in conference road games.
Illinois returns home for a meeting with Minnesota on Saturday, Jan. 17.
